title: OmniFlow service contract: unified generation+embedding+ranks PRD & go-live checks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Define the product contract and acceptance path for a unified API bundle that lets customers call generation (chat/completions), embeddings, and reranking as a cohesive interaction. This PRD clarifies scope, behavior guarantees, performance SLOs, and an operational go-live checklist to minimize regressions and customer confusion.
background: Motivation: Customers building retrieval-augmented generation and rerank pipelines repeatedly stitch together multiple Redwood endpoints. That fragmentation increases integration burden and causes inconsistent behavior across fallbacks, latency SLAs, and billing. OmniFlow bundles a single service contract so clients can declare: generate with context, embed candidate documents, request a rerank pass, and receive coherent scoring/traceability across calls. This ticket codifies the product surface and acceptance criteria for the initial hosted rollout.
goals: 1) Produce a consumable, stable API contract covering gen/emb/rerank interactions with clear input/output schema and error semantics. 2) Deliver a launch readiness checklist for API, SDKs, console docs, and observability. 3) Define SLOs and quality gates (latency, token cost variance, rerank correctness) and an eval harness for preflight checks.
non_goals: 1) Full IAM/RBAC for on-prem installs (out of scope for hosted MVP). 2) Large-language-model training or model discovery flows. 3) Native multimodal embeddings for v1 (text-only embeddings only).
requirements: - API surface: single /omniflow/v1/interaction endpoint with mode attribute to sequence sub-operations (gen->embed->rerank) or run them independently.  - Backwards compatibility: existing generation and embedding endpoints remain stable; OmniFlow must not change behavior of existing endpoints.  - Schema: structured request/response JSON with deterministic request IDs, per-step latency and token usage fields, and optional function/tool-calling plumbing passed through to generation models.  - Observability: per-API-token breakdown, per-step traces, and per-interaction quality metrics available in Console.  - SLOs: 99th percentile latency for single-step gen <= 600ms for short prompts (<256 tokens) on the default quality band; embeddings 99th <= 200ms; rerank 99th <= 500ms for top-100 candidate set.  - Regression safety: auto-block on quality delta > 2% on key eval prompt-set.  - Billing: interactions charge granularly per-step using existing token & embedding pricing schema; must surface an estimated cost pre-execution in SDK for predictable PLG flows.
success_metrics: - Adoption: 20 pilot customers integrate OmniFlow in first 8 weeks. - Latency: Meet SLOs 95% during canary. - Cost predictability: SDK preflight estimate within ±10% of final billed amount for >= 90% of calls. - Quality: no more than 1% of calls trigger a user-facing regression (as flagged by eval suite or customer tickets) in first 30 days.
acceptance_criteria: 1) API: /omniflow/v1/interaction responds with documented schema; request_id present; per-step subresponses available. 2) Backwards compatibility tests: existing /generate and /embeddings endpoints show zero behavioral diffs on regression harness. 3) SDKs: Node and Python SDKs expose interaction builder with preflight cost estimation and streaming generation hooks. 4) Observability: Console dashboard shows per-interaction latency, cost, and rerank-score distributions for the canary tenant. 5) Auto-rollback: deployment pipeline can automatically rollback if eval gates exceed thresholds. 6) Security: API keys and token scoping work with existing rate-limiting and quota systems. 7) Docs: Developer guide, API reference, quickstart sample app, and migration notes published in docs site. 8) E2E tests: deterministic smoke tests passing in staging with seeded models and deterministic RNG for generation when seeded. 9) Pricing clarity: billing preview matches final bill for sample workload (test harness).
launch_checklist: 1) API contract signoff from PM/Eng/Design. 2) SDK releases: Node 3.12.0, Python 2.7.0 with integration tests. 3) Console tile and per-token analytics query added to Console sprint. 4) Canary plan: 5 pilot accounts (internal + paying customers), 48-hour ramp to 5% traffic, 7-day observation window. 5) Eval harness: integration with regression-eval CI with baseline prompts and rerank truth sets. 6) Monitoring: dashboards created, alerts configured for latency, error rate, and quality-delta thresholds. 7) Runbook & incident playbooks written and reviewed. 8) Legal/Compliance: data handling review completed and DPA updated. 9) Billing: cost preview calculation validated against 10M synthetic calls. 10) Support enablement: triage guide and canned responses published for frontline. 11) Training: one live training session for solution engineering.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal dogfood for 2 weeks with feature flags and strict SRE monitoring. Phase 1: Invite-only pilot with 5 customers (apply corrective actions on observed regressions). Phase 2: Soft launch to 5% of free tier / new signups for 7 days. Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 100% over 3 weeks contingent on SLOs and eval stability. Each phase has defined halt criteria (quality delta > 2% or error rate spike > 0.5%).
risks_and_mitigations: - Risk: Consolidated surface may conceal per-step failure modes. Mitigation: per-step error codes and explicit partial-failure semantics; SDKs expose retry/backoff helpers tuned per-step. - Risk: Increased tail latency under multiplexed workloads. Mitigation: conservative canary, separate circuit-breaker for heavy rerank invocations, and autoscaling policy tuned to per-step profiles. - Risk: Billing confusion. Mitigation: SDK preflight estimate + Console billing breakdown per interaction. - Risk: Model drift impacting rerank quality. Mitigation: tie canary to continuous eval suite and require manual override to unfreeze model rollouts.
dependencies: - Runtime: kernel-scheduler v1.12 for improved short-sequence perf. - Observability: trace-enrichment PR in infra repo. - SDK: streaming API changes on Node/Python. - Legal: DPA update and privacy review. - Sales: pilot customer roster and contract addenda for pilot.
notes: Scope decisions and trade-offs logged: 1) Chose single endpoint to reduce round-trip cost for RAG patterns; tradeoff is longer request processing in the runtime. 2) Deferred on-prem RBAC to prioritize hosted speed to market. 3) Limited v1 rerank to top-100 candidate sets to bound cost and latency. Follow-ups: product ticket to add multimodal embeddings, another to support federated billing breakdowns for large tenants.
